terms.definition: A pure substance made of only one kind of atom.
terms.function: The raw ingredient that combines to form compounds and molecules.
terms.whereItIs: The gold, carbon, oxygen, and helium samples in the model.
terms.whyItMatters: About 90 natural elements build everything in the universe.

terms.definition: The number of protons in an atom, which defines its element.
terms.function: Uniquely identifies every element — 6 protons is carbon, 79 is gold.
terms.whereItIs: Identical across all the atoms in each element sample.
terms.whyItMatters: The proton count is the identity card of every element.

terms.definition: A material made of one uniform kind of particle, with fixed properties.
terms.function: Distinguishes elements (one atom type) from mixtures (many types mixed).
terms.whereItIs: Every sample in the model is a pure substance.
terms.whyItMatters: Purity is what makes an element recognizable and predictable.

terms.definition: A pure substance made of different elements chemically bonded.
terms.function: What elements become when they bond — water from hydrogen and oxygen.
terms.whereItIs: The water molecule formed in the combine layer.
terms.whyItMatters: Compounds are how elements build the world's substances.
